```{python}
#| include: false
from IPython.display import HTML, display
import html
import math
import hashlib
import re
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "database_module"))

from db_handler import DbHandler, DbUtils
from db_config import USERNAME, PASSWORD, DATABASE_NAME, HOST, PORT, PGS_EXCEL_FILEPATH

db_handler = DbHandler(
    port=PORT,
    db_url=None,
    user=USERNAME,
    password=PASSWORD,
    host=HOST,
)
db_handler.connect()
db_utils = DbUtils(db_handler)

prsc_id = 3980  # placeholder for testing jobs


# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Resolve the user's primary ancestry.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
ethnicity_query = f"""
SELECT * 
FROM snpster_users.user_ancestry
WHERE user_id = (
    SELECT user_id
    FROM snpster_users.imputation_jobs
    WHERE imputation_id IN (
        SELECT imputation_id
        FROM snpster_users.prsc_jobs
        WHERE prsc_id = {prsc_id}
        LIMIT 1
    )
)
"""

ancestry_df = db_utils.get_pd_dataframe_from_query(ethnicity_query)

if ancestry_df.empty:
    raise ValueError(f"No ancestry record found for prsc_id={prsc_id}.")

primary_ancestry_code = ancestry_df["primary_ancestry"].iloc[0]

if pd.isna(primary_ancestry_code):
    raise ValueError(
        f"Primary ancestry has not been assigned for prsc_id={prsc_id}."
    )

primary_ancestry_code = str(primary_ancestry_code).strip().upper()

# Map SNPster's current ancestry codes onto broad ancestry labels used in
# evaluation_sample_sets.broad_ancestry_category.
#
# The ESS field can contain several comma-separated ancestry labels in one
# value, so the SQL below matches recognized tokens rather than requiring the
# whole field to equal one string. Ambiguous generic ancestry labels are not
# forced into a specific SNPster ancestry component.
#
# AFR is retained as a legacy alias for older records; the current schema uses
# SSA for Sub-Saharan African ancestry.
if primary_ancestry_code == "AFR":
    primary_ancestry_code = "SSA"

ancestry_display_map = {
    "EUR": "European",
    "EAS": "East Asian",
    "SAS": "South Asian",
    "SSA": "Sub-Saharan African",
    "MID": "Greater Middle Eastern",
    "AMR": "Hispanic / Latin American",
    "SEA": "South East Asian",
    "CAS": "Central Asian",
    "NAM": "Native American",
    "OCE": "Oceanian",
}

ancestry_token_map = {
    "EUR": [
        "European",
    ],
    "EAS": [
        "East Asian",
    ],
    "SAS": [
        "South Asian",
    ],
    "SSA": [
        "African unspecified",
        "African American or Afro-Caribbean",
        "Sub-Saharan African",
    ],
    "MID": [
        "Greater Middle Eastern",
        "Greater Middle Eastern (Middle Eastern, North African or Persian)",
    ],
    "AMR": [
        "Hispanic or Latin American",
    ],
    "SEA": [
        "South East Asian",
    ],
    "CAS": [
        "Central Asian",
    ],
    "NAM": [
        "Native American",
    ],
    "OCE": [
        "Oceanian",
    ],
}

if primary_ancestry_code not in ancestry_token_map:
    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported primary ancestry code: {primary_ancestry_code}"
    )

# Validation evidence is not restricted to one population for substantially
# admixed individuals. Any ancestry component above 20% contributes compatible
# evaluation cohorts; the recorded primary ancestry is always retained as a
# fallback even when no component exceeds the threshold.
MIXED_ANCESTRY_VALIDATION_THRESHOLD = 0.20

ancestry_fraction_column_map = {
    "EUR": "eur",
    "EAS": "eas",
    "SAS": "sas",
    "SSA": "ssa",
    "MID": "mid",
    "AMR": "amr",
    "SEA": "sea",
    "CAS": "cas",
    "NAM": "nam",
    "OCE": "oce",
}

ancestry_row = ancestry_df.iloc[0]
ancestry_fraction_by_code = {}

for code, column in ancestry_fraction_column_map.items():
    value = pd.to_numeric(
        pd.Series([ancestry_row.get(column, np.nan)]),
        errors="coerce",
    ).iloc[0]
    if not pd.isna(value):
        ancestry_fraction_by_code[code] = float(value)

selected_validation_ancestry_codes = [primary_ancestry_code]

additional_codes = sorted(
    [
        code
        for code, fraction in ancestry_fraction_by_code.items()
        if fraction > MIXED_ANCESTRY_VALIDATION_THRESHOLD
        and code != primary_ancestry_code
        and code in ancestry_token_map
    ],
    key=lambda code: (
        -ancestry_fraction_by_code.get(code, 0.0),
        code,
    ),
)
selected_validation_ancestry_codes.extend(additional_codes)

ancestry_tokens = []
seen_ancestry_tokens = set()
for code in selected_validation_ancestry_codes:
    for token in ancestry_token_map[code]:
        token_key = token.casefold().strip()
        if token_key and token_key not in seen_ancestry_tokens:
            seen_ancestry_tokens.add(token_key)
            ancestry_tokens.append(token)

ethnicity = " + ".join(
    ancestry_display_map[code]
    for code in selected_validation_ancestry_codes
)

# These labels are fixed application constants, but quote them defensively
# before embedding them into the SQL ARRAY literal.
ethnicity_sql = ethnicity.replace("'", "''")
ancestry_tokens_sql = ", ".join(
    "'" + token.replace("'", "''").lower() + "'"
    for token in ancestry_tokens
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. Resolve report identity and generation metadata.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
report_job_query = f"""
SELECT ij.*
FROM snpster_users.prsc_jobs AS pj
JOIN snpster_users.imputation_jobs AS ij
    ON ij.imputation_id = pj.imputation_id
WHERE pj.prsc_id = {prsc_id}
LIMIT 1
"""

report_job_df = db_utils.get_pd_dataframe_from_query(report_job_query)

if report_job_df.empty:
    raise ValueError(
        f"No imputation-job context found for prsc_id={prsc_id}."
    )

report_job_row = report_job_df.iloc[0]
report_user_id = str(report_job_row.get("user_id", "Unknown profile")).strip()
report_user_id_sql = report_user_id.replace("'", "''")

report_imputation_id = int(report_job_row["imputation_id"])

report_sections_query = """
SELECT DISTINCT BTRIM(report_name) AS report_name
FROM snpster_users.pgs_reports_shop
WHERE NULLIF(BTRIM(report_name), '') IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY BTRIM(report_name)
"""

report_sections_df = db_utils.get_pd_dataframe_from_query(report_sections_query)

report_section_names = (
    report_sections_df["report_name"]
    .dropna()
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
    .loc[lambda values: values.ne("")]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .tolist()
)


def first_nonempty_value(row, candidates):
    """Return the first non-empty value from candidate columns."""
    if row is None:
        return None

    for column in candidates:
        if column not in row.index:
            continue

        value = row[column]

        if pd.isna(value):
            continue

        value = str(value).strip()

        if value:
            return value

    return None


try:
    report_profile_query = f"""
    SELECT *
    FROM snpster_users.user_information
    WHERE user_id = '{report_user_id_sql}'
    LIMIT 1
    """
    report_profile_df = db_utils.get_pd_dataframe_from_query(
        report_profile_query
    )
except Exception:
    report_profile_df = pd.DataFrame()

report_profile_row = (
    report_profile_df.iloc[0]
    if not report_profile_df.empty
    else None
)

report_full_name = first_nonempty_value(
    report_profile_row,
    [
        "full_name",
        "display_name",
        "name",
        "user_name",
        "username",
    ],
)

if report_full_name is None:
    report_first_name = first_nonempty_value(
        report_profile_row,
        ["first_name", "firstname", "given_name"],
    )
    report_last_name = first_nonempty_value(
        report_profile_row,
        ["last_name", "lastname", "family_name", "surname"],
    )
    report_full_name = " ".join(
        value
        for value in [report_first_name, report_last_name]
        if value
    ).strip()

if not report_full_name:
    report_full_name = report_user_id

report_data_source = first_nonempty_value(
    report_job_row,
    [
        "data_source",
        "genotyping_vendor",
        "vendor",
        "source_vendor",
        "file_provider",
        "input_vendor",
        "provider",
    ],
)

if report_data_source is None:
    report_data_source = "Uploaded genotype data"

report_now = datetime.now()
report_date = (
    f"{report_now.strftime('%B')} {report_now.day}, {report_now.year}"
)
report_identifier = f"SNPSTER-{prsc_id}"
report_version = "1.0"


# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Find PSS IDs relevant to that ancestry, then use those PSS IDs
#    to retrieve their PPM performance rows.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
query = f"""
WITH latest_user_results AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (pjr.pgs_id)
        pjr.*
    FROM snpster_users.prsc_job_results AS pjr
    INNER JOIN snpster_users.prsc_jobs AS pj
        ON pj.prsc_id = pjr.prsc_id
    WHERE pj.imputation_id = {report_imputation_id}
      AND pj.prsc_status = 'completed'
    ORDER BY
        pjr.pgs_id,
        COALESCE(pj.completed_at, pj.started_at, pj.created_at) DESC,
        pj.prsc_id DESC
),

ancestry_matched_ess AS (
    SELECT ess.*
    FROM data_libraries.evaluation_sample_sets AS ess
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM unnest(
            string_to_array(
                COALESCE(ess.broad_ancestry_category, ''),
                ','
            )
        ) AS ancestry_token(value)
        WHERE lower(btrim(ancestry_token.value)) = ANY (
            ARRAY[{ancestry_tokens_sql}]::text[]
        )
    )
),

ancestry_matched_pss AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pgs_id,
        pss_id
    FROM ancestry_matched_ess
),

ancestry_matched_pss_stats AS (
    SELECT
        pgs_id,
        pss_id,

        SUM(
            COALESCE(
                individuals_evaluation,
                COALESCE(cases_evaluation, 0)
                + COALESCE(controls_evaluation, 0)
            )
        ) AS individuals_evaluation,

        SUM(cases_evaluation) AS cases_evaluation,
        SUM(controls_evaluation) AS controls_evaluation

    FROM ancestry_matched_ess

    GROUP BY
        pgs_id,
        pss_id
),

matched_pss_metadata AS (
    SELECT
        matched.pgs_id,
        matched.pss_id,

        STRING_AGG(
            DISTINCT NULLIF(BTRIM(ess.cohort), ''),
            ' / '
            ORDER BY NULLIF(BTRIM(ess.cohort), '')
        ) AS cohort

    FROM ancestry_matched_pss AS matched

    LEFT JOIN data_libraries.evaluation_sample_sets AS ess
        ON BTRIM(ess.pss_id) = BTRIM(matched.pss_id)
       AND BTRIM(ess.pgs_id) = BTRIM(matched.pgs_id)

    GROUP BY
        matched.pgs_id,
        matched.pss_id
)

SELECT
    pjr.pgs_id,
    BTRIM(shop.report_name) AS report_name,

    CASE
        WHEN pcd.reported_trait IN (
            'Coronary artery disease',
            'Coronary Artery Disease'
        )
            THEN 'Coronary heart disease'

        WHEN pcd.reported_trait = 'Type 1 diabetes (T1D)'
            THEN 'Type 1 diabetes'

        WHEN pcd.reported_trait = 'Asthma (diagnosed by doctor)'
            THEN 'Asthma'

        WHEN pcd.reported_trait IN (
            'Type 2 diabetes (T2D)',
            'Type 2 diabetes (based on SNPs involved in β-cell function)'
        )
            THEN 'Type 2 diabetes'

        WHEN pcd.reported_trait = 'Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)'
            THEN 'Inflammatory bowel disease'

        WHEN pcd.reported_trait IN (
            'Type 2 diabetes (based on SNPs involved in insulin secretion)',
            'Type 2 diabetes (based on SNPs associated with insulin secretion)'
        )
            THEN 'Type 2 diabetes'

        ELSE pcd.reported_trait
    END AS reported_trait,

    pcd.reported_trait AS source_reported_trait,
    pcd.mapped_trait_efo_label,
    pcd.efo_id,
    pp.reported_trait AS specific_trait,

    pjr.percentile_most_similar_pop,
    pjr.z_most_similar_pop,
    pjr.z_norm1,
    pjr.z_norm2,
    pjr.percent_variants_matched,
    pjr.n_variants_matched,

    pp.ppm_id,
    pp.pss_id,
    pp.pgp_id,

    pss_stats.individuals_evaluation,
    pss_stats.cases_evaluation,
    pss_stats.controls_evaluation,
    pss_metadata.cohort,
    '{ethnicity_sql}' AS broad_ancestry_category,

    pp.pgs_performance_other_relevant_info,
    pp.publication_pmid,
    pp.publication_doi,

    pp.hazard_ratio,
    pp.odds_ratio,
    pp.beta,
    pp.auroc,
    pp.concordance_statistic,

    pub.first_author,
    pub.title,
    pub.journal_name,
    pub.publication_date,
    pub.release_date AS publication_release_date,
    pub.authors,
    pub.pubmed_id_pmid,
    pub.digital_object_identifier_doi,

    pcd.publication_pmid AS development_publication_pmid,
    pcd.publication_doi AS development_publication_doi,
    pcd.pgp_id AS development_pgp_id,
    pcd.number_of_variants,
    pcd.original_genome_build,
    pcd.type_of_variant_weight,
    pcd.pgs_development_method,
    pcd.release_date AS pgs_release_date

FROM latest_user_results AS pjr

INNER JOIN snpster_users.pgs_reports_shop AS shop
    ON shop.pgs_id = pjr.pgs_id

INNER JOIN data_libraries.pgscatalog_data AS pcd
    ON pcd.pgs_id = pjr.pgs_id

-- Step 1: retain PSS IDs matching the selected validation ancestries.
INNER JOIN ancestry_matched_pss AS matched_pss
    ON matched_pss.pgs_id = pjr.pgs_id

-- Step 2: use those PSS IDs to retrieve the associated PPM records.
INNER JOIN data_libraries.pgs_performance AS pp
    ON pp.pgs_id = matched_pss.pgs_id
   AND pp.pss_id = matched_pss.pss_id

-- Descriptive sample-size metadata for the already-selected ancestry rows.
LEFT JOIN ancestry_matched_pss_stats AS pss_stats
    ON pss_stats.pgs_id = matched_pss.pgs_id
   AND pss_stats.pss_id = matched_pss.pss_id

LEFT JOIN matched_pss_metadata AS pss_metadata
    ON pss_metadata.pgs_id = matched_pss.pgs_id
   AND pss_metadata.pss_id = matched_pss.pss_id

LEFT JOIN data_libraries.pgs_publications AS pub
    ON pub.pgp_id = pp.pgp_id

ORDER BY
    BTRIM(shop.report_name),
    reported_trait,
    pjr.pgs_id,
    pss_stats.individuals_evaluation DESC,
    pp.ppm_id;
"""

data = db_utils.get_pd_dataframe_from_query(query)
data = data.drop_duplicates()

MIN_PRIMARY_VARIANT_MATCH_PCT = 70.0
```

```{python}
#| include: false
def risk_level(percentile):
    """Five-category percentile classification based on the selected best model.

    Thresholds can be tuned later, but these are simple launch defaults:
      <5   = Very low
      5-19 = Lowered
      20-79 = Normal
      80-94 = Increased
      >=95 = Highly Increased
    """
    if pd.isna(percentile):
        return ("Unknown", "normal", "fill-normal")

    percentile = float(percentile)

    if percentile >= 95:
        return ("Highly Increased", "highly-increased", "fill-highly-increased")
    if percentile >= 80:
        return ("Increased", "increased", "fill-increased")
    if percentile >= 20:
        return ("Normal", "normal", "fill-normal")
    if percentile >= 5:
        return ("Lowered", "lowered", "fill-lowered")
    return ("Very low", "very-low", "fill-very-low")


def ordinal_suffix(n):
    n = int(n)
    if 10 <= (n % 100) <= 20:
        return "th"
    return {1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd"}.get(n % 10, "th")


def fmt_percentile(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return "Not available"
    n = int(round(float(x)))
    return f"{n}{ordinal_suffix(n)}"


def fmt_percentile_range(low, high):
    if pd.isna(low) or pd.isna(high):
        return None

    low_i = int(round(float(low)))
    high_i = int(round(float(high)))

    if low_i == high_i:
        return fmt_percentile(low_i)

    return f"{fmt_percentile(low_i)}–{fmt_percentile(high_i)}"


def clamp_percentile(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return 0.0
    return max(0.0, min(100.0, float(x)))


def z_to_percentile(z):
    """Convert a standard-normal z-score to a 0-100 percentile."""
    if z is None or pd.isna(z):
        return np.nan

    z = float(z)
    probability = 0.5 * (
        1.0 + math.erf(z / math.sqrt(2.0))
    )
    return max(0.0, min(100.0, probability * 100.0))


def display_percentile_for_column(primary, all_models, column):
    """Use the report's existing display rule for any percentile source.

    With >4 retained models, show the median across models. Otherwise show the
    selected primary PGS value, falling back to the median if that value is
    unavailable.
    """
    if all_models is None or all_models.empty:
        return np.nan

    if column not in all_models.columns:
        return np.nan

    values = pd.to_numeric(
        all_models[column],
        errors="coerce",
    ).dropna()

    if len(values) > 4:
        return float(values.median())

    primary_value = (
        primary.get(column, np.nan)
        if primary is not None
        else np.nan
    )

    if primary_value is not None and not pd.isna(primary_value):
        return float(primary_value)

    if not values.empty:
        return float(values.median())

    return np.nan


def fmt_float(x, digits=2):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return None
    return f"{float(x):.{digits}f}"


def fmt_int(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return None
    return f"{int(float(x)):,}"


def variant_match_percent_value(x):
    """Return variant match as a 0-100 percentage for filtering/ranking."""
    if pd.isna(x):
        return np.nan

    x = float(x)
    if x <= 1:
        x = x * 100
    return x


def fmt_variant_match_pct(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return None

    x = variant_match_percent_value(x)
    return f"{x:.1f}%"


def fmt_variant_match_summary(row):
    if row is None:
        return None

    pct = fmt_variant_match_pct(row.get("percent_variants_matched", np.nan))
    n = fmt_int(row.get("n_variants_matched", np.nan))

    if pct and n:
        return f"{pct} ({n} variants)"
    if pct:
        return pct
    if n:
        return f"{n} variants"
    return None


def fmt_date(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return None
    return str(pd.to_datetime(x).date())


def safe_text(x, fallback="Not available"):
    if x is None or pd.isna(x) or str(x).strip() == "":
        return fallback
    return html.escape(str(x))


def shorten(text, n=170):
    if text is None or pd.isna(text):
        return None
    text = str(text).strip()
    if len(text) <= n:
        return text
    return text[: n - 1].rstrip() + "…"


def get_eval_n(row):
    if not pd.isna(row.get("individuals_evaluation", np.nan)):
        return float(row["individuals_evaluation"])

    cases = 0 if pd.isna(row.get("cases_evaluation", np.nan)) else float(row["cases_evaluation"])
    controls = 0 if pd.isna(row.get("controls_evaluation", np.nan)) else float(row["controls_evaluation"])
    total = cases + controls
    return total if total > 0 else np.nan


def add_ranking_columns(df):
    """Prepare PPM rows that already passed the exact primary-ancestry PSS filter."""
    df = df.copy()

    numeric_columns = [
        "auroc",
        "concordance_statistic",
        "percentile_most_similar_pop",
        "z_most_similar_pop",
        "z_norm1",
        "z_norm2",
        "odds_ratio",
        "hazard_ratio",
        "individuals_evaluation",
        "cases_evaluation",
        "controls_evaluation",
        "percent_variants_matched",
        "n_variants_matched",
    ]

    for col in numeric_columns:
        if col in df.columns:
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

    # Norm 2 is the report's canonical percentile normalization because it is
    # more appropriate for individuals who do not sit cleanly inside a single
    # reference-population cluster. Norm 1 and closest-population normalization
    # remain visible as secondary context.
    df["percentile_norm1"] = df["z_norm1"].apply(z_to_percentile)
    df["percentile_norm2"] = df["z_norm2"].apply(z_to_percentile)

    df["evaluation_n"] = df.apply(get_eval_n, axis=1)

    # Prefer AUROC when available, otherwise use the concordance statistic.
    # The source metric type is retained so the card can label it correctly.
    df["discrimination_value"] = df["auroc"].combine_first(
        df["concordance_statistic"]
    )
    df["discrimination_metric"] = np.select(
        [
            df["auroc"].notna(),
            df["concordance_statistic"].notna(),
        ],
        [
            "AUROC",
            "Concordance statistic",
        ],
        default=None,
    )

    df["variant_match_pct_for_ranking"] = (
        df["percent_variants_matched"].apply(variant_match_percent_value)
    )
    df["primary_model_eligible"] = (
        df["variant_match_pct_for_ranking"].ge(
            MIN_PRIMARY_VARIANT_MATCH_PCT
        )
    )

    # User-specific percent change, not the raw OR/HR per SD.
    # This assumes OR/HR are reported per 1 SD increase in PRS.
    df["individual_odds_ratio"] = np.where(
        df["odds_ratio"].notna() & df["z_norm2"].notna(),
        ((df["odds_ratio"] ** df["z_norm2"]) - 1) * 100,
        np.nan,
    )

    df["individual_hazard_ratio"] = np.where(
        df["hazard_ratio"].notna() & df["z_norm2"].notna(),
        ((df["hazard_ratio"] ** df["z_norm2"]) - 1) * 100,
        np.nan,
    )

    return df


def normalize_pmid_value(value):
    """Return a stable string representation of a PMID."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    text_value = str(value).strip()
    if not text_value:
        return None

    try:
        numeric = float(text_value)
        if numeric.is_integer():
            return str(int(numeric))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        pass

    return text_value



def normalize_doi_value(value):
    """Return a stable DOI without URL or 'doi:' prefixes."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    doi = str(value).strip()
    if not doi:
        return None

    doi = re.sub(
        r"^(?:https?://(?:dx\.)?doi\.org/|doi:\s*)",
        "",
        doi,
        flags=re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    doi = doi.strip().rstrip(".,;")
    return doi.lower() if doi else None


def publication_reference_value(
    pmid,
    doi,
    fallback_pmid=None,
    fallback_doi=None,
):
    """Display PMID when available, otherwise DOI."""
    normalized_pmid = normalize_pmid_value(pmid)
    if normalized_pmid:
        return f"PMID: {normalized_pmid}"

    normalized_doi = normalize_doi_value(doi)
    if normalized_doi:
        return f"DOI: {normalized_doi}"

    normalized_fallback_pmid = normalize_pmid_value(fallback_pmid)
    if normalized_fallback_pmid:
        return f"PMID: {normalized_fallback_pmid}"

    normalized_fallback_doi = normalize_doi_value(fallback_doi)
    if normalized_fallback_doi:
        return f"DOI: {normalized_fallback_doi}"

    return None


def publication_identifier_for_row(row):
    """Canonical publication key for an ancestry-matched PERFORMANCE record.

    Prefer the PGS Catalog performance-publication ID (PGP ID). Fall back to
    the publication identifiers carried by the PPM record. Deliberately do not
    fall back to the PGS development publication, because the Publications orb
    is intended to count publications contributing the retained validation
    evidence rather than unrelated development-paper metadata.
    """
    if row is None:
        return None

    pgp_id = row.get("pgp_id", np.nan)
    if pgp_id is not None and not pd.isna(pgp_id):
        pgp_id = str(pgp_id).strip()
        if pgp_id:
            return f"pgp:{pgp_id}".lower()

    joined_pmid = normalize_pmid_value(
        row.get("pubmed_id_pmid", np.nan)
    )
    if joined_pmid:
        return f"pmid:{joined_pmid}".lower()

    joined_doi = normalize_doi_value(
        row.get("digital_object_identifier_doi", np.nan)
    )
    if joined_doi:
        return f"doi:{joined_doi}".lower()

    publication_pmid = normalize_pmid_value(
        row.get("publication_pmid", np.nan)
    )
    if publication_pmid:
        return f"pmid:{publication_pmid}".lower()

    publication_doi = normalize_doi_value(
        row.get("publication_doi", np.nan)
    )
    if publication_doi:
        return f"doi:{publication_doi}".lower()

    return None


def count_unique_publications(df):
    """Count distinct publications identified by PMID or DOI."""
    if df is None or df.empty:
        return 0

    identifiers = df.apply(
        publication_identifier_for_row,
        axis=1,
    )
    identifiers = identifiers.dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
    identifiers = identifiers[identifiers.ne("")]
    return int(identifiers.nunique())


STUDY_COLOR_PALETTE = [
    "#5B8DC5", "#C4778A", "#5FA083", "#B88A4A",
    "#7C70B5", "#4F9BA7", "#C27652", "#829A50",
    "#A06D9B", "#6B88A7", "#B56F5E", "#638D71",
]


def study_color(study_key):
    """Return a deterministic color for a publication/study identifier."""
    if study_key is None or not str(study_key).strip():
        return "#6B7280"

    digest = hashlib.sha1(
        str(study_key).strip().casefold().encode("utf-8")
    ).hexdigest()
    index = int(digest[:8], 16) % len(STUDY_COLOR_PALETTE)
    return STUDY_COLOR_PALETTE[index]


def development_study_identity(row):
    """Study identity for a PGS percentile point."""
    pmid = normalize_pmid_value(
        row.get("development_publication_pmid", np.nan)
    )
    if pmid:
        return f"pmid:{pmid}", f"PMID {pmid}"

    doi = normalize_doi_value(
        row.get("development_publication_doi", np.nan)
    )
    if doi:
        return f"doi:{doi}", f"DOI {doi}"

    pgp_id = row.get("development_pgp_id", np.nan)
    if pgp_id is not None and not pd.isna(pgp_id):
        pgp_id = str(pgp_id).strip()
        if pgp_id:
            return f"pgp:{pgp_id}", pgp_id

    return None, "Study not available"


def performance_study_identity(row):
    """Study identity for a validation/effect point."""
    pmid = normalize_pmid_value(row.get("pubmed_id_pmid", np.nan))
    if not pmid:
        pmid = normalize_pmid_value(row.get("publication_pmid", np.nan))
    if pmid:
        return f"pmid:{pmid}", f"PMID {pmid}"

    doi = normalize_doi_value(row.get("digital_object_identifier_doi", np.nan))
    if not doi:
        doi = normalize_doi_value(row.get("publication_doi", np.nan))
    if doi:
        return f"doi:{doi}", f"DOI {doi}"

    pgp_id = row.get("pgp_id", np.nan)
    if pgp_id is not None and not pd.isna(pgp_id):
        pgp_id = str(pgp_id).strip()
        if pgp_id:
            return f"pgp:{pgp_id}", pgp_id

    return None, "Study not available"



def stable_method_family_id(pmid, reported_trait, development_method):
    """Create a deterministic descriptive family ID from PMID + trait + development method."""
    canonical = "||".join([
        str(pmid),
        str(reported_trait).strip(),
        str(development_method).strip(),
    ])
    digest = hashlib.sha1(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8].upper()
    return f"FAM_{pmid}_{digest}"


def singleton_family_id(pgs_id):
    """Create a deterministic singleton family ID for one PGS."""
    return f"FAM_{str(pgs_id).strip()}"


def assign_report_family_ids(df):
    """Assign descriptive model-lineage family IDs without changing report scoring.

    Rules:
      1. Work within each PGS development PMID + reported_trait group.
      2. If the group contains only 1 unique PGS ID, that PGS is a singleton family.
      3. If the group contains >1 unique PGS IDs:
         - PGS IDs with the same non-missing pgs_development_method share a family ID.
         - Different development methods receive different family IDs.
         - Missing development methods are kept as singleton families.

    These family IDs are descriptive metadata only. They are NOT used for scoring,
    aggregation, weighting, or primary-model selection.
    """
    df = df.copy()

    # Family lineage must be based on the PGS DEVELOPMENT publication,
    # not on whichever external publication supplied the selected PPM.
    df["family_pmid"] = df["development_publication_pmid"].apply(
        normalize_pmid_value
    )

    df["family_id"] = None
    df["family_grouping_rule"] = None

    for (pmid, trait), group in df.groupby(
        ["family_pmid", "reported_trait"],
        dropna=False,
        sort=False,
    ):
        unique_pgs_ids = [
            str(x).strip()
            for x in group["pgs_id"].dropna().unique().tolist()
        ]

        # One PGS only, or no usable PMID: keep singleton.
        if pd.isna(pmid) or pmid is None or len(unique_pgs_ids) <= 1:
            for pgs_id in unique_pgs_ids:
                mask = group["pgs_id"].astype(str).eq(pgs_id)
                indices = group.index[mask]
                df.loc[indices, "family_id"] = singleton_family_id(pgs_id)
                df.loc[indices, "family_grouping_rule"] = (
                    "Singleton family: development-PMID/trait group contains only one PGS ID "
                    "or no usable PMID."
                )
            continue

        # Resolve one non-missing development method per PGS ID.
        pgs_method_map = {}
        for pgs_id, pgs_rows in group.groupby("pgs_id", sort=False):
            methods = (
                pgs_rows["pgs_development_method"]
                .dropna()
                .astype(str)
                .str.strip()
            )
            methods = methods[methods.ne("")]
            method = methods.iloc[0] if not methods.empty else None
            pgs_method_map[str(pgs_id).strip()] = method

        method_to_pgs = {}
        missing_method_pgs = []

        for pgs_id, method in pgs_method_map.items():
            if method is None:
                missing_method_pgs.append(pgs_id)
            else:
                method_to_pgs.setdefault(method, []).append(pgs_id)

        # Same PMID + trait + development method => same descriptive family ID.
        for method, pgs_ids in method_to_pgs.items():
            family_id = stable_method_family_id(pmid, trait, method)
            mask = group["pgs_id"].astype(str).isin(pgs_ids)
            indices = group.index[mask]
            df.loc[indices, "family_id"] = family_id
            df.loc[indices, "family_grouping_rule"] = (
                f"Descriptive lineage grouping within development PMID {pmid} and trait '{trait}' "
                f"using pgs_development_method='{method}'."
            )

        # Missing method: do not infer grouping.
        for pgs_id in missing_method_pgs:
            mask = group["pgs_id"].astype(str).eq(pgs_id)
            indices = group.index[mask]
            df.loc[indices, "family_id"] = singleton_family_id(pgs_id)
            df.loc[indices, "family_grouping_rule"] = (
                "Singleton family: development method is missing."
            )

    # Safety fallback.
    missing_family = df["family_id"].isna()
    if missing_family.any():
        df.loc[missing_family, "family_id"] = df.loc[
            missing_family, "pgs_id"
        ].apply(singleton_family_id)
        df.loc[missing_family, "family_grouping_rule"] = (
            "Singleton family: fallback assignment."
        )

    family_sizes = (
        df.groupby("family_id")["pgs_id"]
        .nunique()
        .to_dict()
    )
    df["family_size"] = df["family_id"].map(family_sizes).fillna(1).astype(int)

    return df


def summarize_pgs_evaluations(pgs_df):
    """Create one PGS-level row while preserving all PPM rows separately.

    Percentile, z-score, and variant-match fields are user/PGS-level values and
    are therefore represented once per PGS.

    Validation discrimination is summarized across ALL ancestry-matched PPMs
    for the PGS. For each PPM, AUROC is used when reported; otherwise the
    concordance statistic is used. The PGS-level discrimination value is the
    arithmetic mean of those available PPM-level discrimination values.

    This summary row is used for percentile agreement, primary-PGS ranking,
    variant-match display, and quality weighting. It is NOT used to discard
    PPM-level OR/HR evidence.
    """
    if pgs_df is None or pgs_df.empty:
        return None

    # Stable representative row for PGS-level metadata that is duplicated
    # across PPM rows (percentile, z-score, variant match, development metadata).
    representative = (
        pgs_df.sort_values(
            by=["ppm_id", "pss_id"],
            ascending=[True, True],
            na_position="last",
        )
        .iloc[0]
        .copy()
    )

    discrimination_values = pd.to_numeric(
        pgs_df["discrimination_value"],
        errors="coerce",
    ).dropna()

    metric_types = (
        pgs_df.loc[
            pgs_df["discrimination_value"].notna(),
            "discrimination_metric",
        ]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .unique()
        .tolist()
    )

    if discrimination_values.empty:
        mean_discrimination = np.nan
        discrimination_label = None
    else:
        mean_discrimination = float(discrimination_values.mean())

        if metric_types == ["AUROC"]:
            discrimination_label = "Mean AUROC"
        elif metric_types == ["Concordance statistic"]:
            discrimination_label = "Mean concordance statistic"
        else:
            discrimination_label = "Mean AUROC / concordance"

    evaluation_n_values = pd.to_numeric(
        pgs_df["evaluation_n"],
        errors="coerce",
    )

    representative["discrimination_value"] = mean_discrimination
    representative["discrimination_metric"] = discrimination_label
    representative["mean_auroc"] = pd.to_numeric(
        pgs_df["auroc"],
        errors="coerce",
    ).mean()
    representative["mean_concordance"] = pd.to_numeric(
        pgs_df["concordance_statistic"],
        errors="coerce",
    ).mean()
    representative["n_discrimination_ppms"] = int(
        discrimination_values.shape[0]
    )
    representative["n_ppm_evaluations"] = int(
        pgs_df["ppm_id"].dropna().nunique()
    )
    representative["n_pss_evaluations"] = int(
        pgs_df["pss_id"].dropna().nunique()
    )
    representative["evaluation_n"] = (
        float(evaluation_n_values.max())
        if evaluation_n_values.notna().any()
        else np.nan
    )

    # A PGS summary is deliberately not tied to one particular PPM/PSS.
    representative["ppm_id"] = np.nan
    representative["pss_id"] = np.nan
    representative["specific_trait"] = np.nan
    representative["auroc"] = np.nan
    representative["concordance_statistic"] = np.nan
    representative["odds_ratio"] = np.nan
    representative["hazard_ratio"] = np.nan
    representative["individual_odds_ratio"] = np.nan
    representative["individual_hazard_ratio"] = np.nan

    return representative


def summarize_rows_per_pgs(df):
    """Return exactly one PGS-level summary row per retained PGS ID."""
    rows = []

    for _, pgs_df in df.groupby("pgs_id", sort=False):
        row = summarize_pgs_evaluations(pgs_df)
        if row is not None:
            rows.append(row)

    if not rows:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=df.columns)

    return pd.DataFrame(rows).reset_index(drop=True)


def sort_for_primary_model(df):
    """Rank distinct PGS models using their mean ancestry-matched validation discrimination.

    Each PGS first receives one mean discrimination value across its available
    ancestry-matched PPMs. This avoids selecting a PGS simply because one
    particular PPM happened to report an unusually favorable value.
    """
    return df.sort_values(
        by=[
            "discrimination_value",
            "evaluation_n",
            "pgs_id",
        ],
        ascending=[False, False, True],
        na_position="last",
    )


def eligible_for_primary(df):
    """Return models passing the report-wide variant-match threshold."""
    return df[df["primary_model_eligible"].fillna(False)].copy()


def best_primary_model_row(df, require_primary_eligible=False):
    if df.empty:
        return None

    if require_primary_eligible:
        df = eligible_for_primary(df)
        if df.empty:
            return None

    return sort_for_primary_model(df).iloc[0]


def valid_metric_ppms(trait_ppms, metric_col, retained_pgs_ids):
    """Return every ancestry-matched PPM with the requested individualized effect.

    The PGS itself must be retained by report-wide QC, but no PPM is collapsed
    merely because the same PGS has several stratified performance endpoints.
    """
    if trait_ppms is None or trait_ppms.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            columns=trait_ppms.columns
            if trait_ppms is not None
            else []
        )

    retained_ids = {str(x) for x in retained_pgs_ids}

    return trait_ppms[
        trait_ppms["pgs_id"].astype(str).isin(retained_ids)
        & trait_ppms["primary_model_eligible"].fillna(False)
        & trait_ppms[metric_col].notna()
    ].copy()


def percent_change_text(x):
    """Display individualized percent change derived from OR/HR and user z-score."""
    if pd.isna(x):
        return "NA"

    x = float(x)
    if abs(x) < 0.05:
        return "No material change"

    direction = "higher" if x > 0 else "lower"
    return f"{abs(x):.1f}% {direction}"


def effect_per_sd_text(row, raw_col, label):
    """Display the published per-SD OR/HR as a caption under the individualized % value."""
    if row is None:
        return f"{label} per SD NA"

    raw = row.get(raw_col, np.nan)
    if pd.isna(raw):
        return f"{label} per SD NA"

    return f"{label} per SD {float(raw):.2f}"


def effect_source_caption(row, raw_col, label):
    """Caption shown under the odds/hazard percent-change metric box."""
    return effect_per_sd_text(row, raw_col, label)


def summarize_individual_effects(models_df, metric_col):
    """Summarize individualized OR/HR effects and calculate the SNPster mean.

    Ordinary median, IQR, and observed range remain unweighted.

    The SNPster mean is used only for odds- and hazard-based effects. Each
    performance estimate receives raw weight:

        (1 / model-family size)
        × PPM-specific AUROC or concordance statistic
        × matched-variant fraction
    """
    if (
        models_df is None
        or models_df.empty
        or metric_col not in models_df.columns
    ):
        return None

    df = models_df.copy()
    df["effect_numeric"] = pd.to_numeric(
        df[metric_col],
        errors="coerce",
    )
    df = df[df["effect_numeric"].notna()].copy()

    if df.empty:
        return None

    values = df["effect_numeric"].astype(float)

    family_size = pd.to_numeric(
        df.get(
            "family_size",
            pd.Series(np.nan, index=df.index),
        ),
        errors="coerce",
    )

    if "family_id" in df.columns and "pgs_id" in df.columns:
        valid_family = (
            df["family_id"].notna()
            & df["family_id"].astype(str).str.strip().ne("")
        )
        fallback_ids = "PGS_SINGLETON_" + df["pgs_id"].astype(str)
        weighted_family_id = df["family_id"].where(
            valid_family,
            fallback_ids,
        )
        fallback_family_size = (
            df.assign(_weighted_family_id=weighted_family_id)
            .groupby("_weighted_family_id")["pgs_id"]
            .transform("nunique")
            .clip(lower=1)
            .astype(float)
        )
    else:
        fallback_family_size = pd.Series(1.0, index=df.index)

    family_size = family_size.where(
        family_size.notna() & family_size.gt(0),
        fallback_family_size,
    )

    family_balance_weight = 1.0 / family_size.astype(float)

    discrimination_weight = pd.to_numeric(
        df.get(
            "discrimination_value",
            pd.Series(np.nan, index=df.index),
        ),
        errors="coerce",
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    variant_match_weight = (
        pd.to_numeric(
            df.get(
                "percent_variants_matched",
                pd.Series(np.nan, index=df.index),
            ),
            errors="coerce",
        )
        .apply(variant_match_percent_value)
        .div(100.0)
        .clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    )

    combined_weight = (
        family_balance_weight
        * discrimination_weight
        * variant_match_weight
    )

    valid_weight = combined_weight.notna() & combined_weight.gt(0)

    if valid_weight.any():
        snpster_mean = float(
            np.average(
                df.loc[valid_weight, "effect_numeric"].astype(float),
                weights=combined_weight.loc[valid_weight].astype(float),
            )
        )
        n_weighted_estimates = int(valid_weight.sum())
    else:
        snpster_mean = np.nan
        n_weighted_estimates = 0

    return {
        "n": int(len(values)),
        "values": values.tolist(),
        "median": float(values.median()),
        "mean": float(values.mean()),
        "snpster_mean": snpster_mean,
        "n_weighted_estimates": n_weighted_estimates,
        "q1": float(values.quantile(0.25)),
        "q3": float(values.quantile(0.75)),
        "min": float(values.min()),
        "max": float(values.max()),
    }



def effect_interval_text(low, high):
    """Human-readable range/IQR that preserves direction around zero."""
    low = float(low)
    high = float(high)

    if low >= 0 and high >= 0:
        return f"{abs(low):.1f}–{abs(high):.1f}% higher"

    if low <= 0 and high <= 0:
        # low is more negative, so reverse absolute values for readable ascending magnitude.
        return f"{abs(high):.1f}–{abs(low):.1f}% lower"

    return f"{abs(low):.1f}% lower to {abs(high):.1f}% higher"


def effect_summary_display(models_df, metric_col, raw_col, ratio_label):
    """Return the median effect with only decision-useful supporting text."""
    stats = summarize_individual_effects(models_df, metric_col)

    if stats is None:
        return "NA", f"{ratio_label} per SD NA", None

    n = stats["n"]
    value = percent_change_text(stats["median"])

    if n == 1:
        row = models_df.loc[
            pd.to_numeric(
                models_df[metric_col],
                errors="coerce",
            ).notna()
        ].iloc[0]
        return (
            value,
            effect_per_sd_text(row, raw_col, ratio_label),
            stats,
        )

    caption_parts = []

    if n == 2:
        caption_parts.append(
            f"Range {effect_interval_text(stats['min'], stats['max'])}"
        )
    else:
        caption_parts.append(
            f"IQR {effect_interval_text(stats['q1'], stats['q3'])}"
        )

    if not pd.isna(stats["snpster_mean"]):
        caption_parts.append(
            "SNPster weighted mean "
            f"{percent_change_text(stats['snpster_mean'])}"
        )

    return value, " · ".join(caption_parts), stats



def effect_axis_label(x):
    """Compact signed label for the mini effect-distribution axis."""
    x = float(x)
    if abs(x) < 0.05:
        return "0%"
    return f"{x:+.1f}%"


def effect_axis_tick_text(x):
    """Compact signed percentage for an effect bar x-axis."""
    x = float(x)

    if abs(x) < 0.05:
        return "0%"

    if abs(x) >= 10:
        return f"{x:+.0f}%"

    return f"{x:+.1f}%"


def effect_axis_labels(axis_low, axis_high):
    """Five evenly spaced x-axis labels beneath an individualized effect bar."""
    ticks = np.linspace(float(axis_low), float(axis_high), 5)
    labels = []

    for i, value in enumerate(ticks):
        position = i * 25.0
        edge_class = ""
        if i == 0:
            edge_class = " edge-left"
        elif i == len(ticks) - 1:
            edge_class = " edge-right"

        labels.append(
            f'<span class="scale-axis-label{edge_class}" '
            f'style="left: {position:.1f}%;">{effect_axis_tick_text(value)}</span>'
        )

    return f"""
    <div class="scale-axis-labels" aria-label="Individualized percentage change axis">
      {''.join(labels)}
    </div>
    """


def make_effect_distribution(models_df, metric_col, metric_name):
    """OR/HR bar with individual estimates, median, and SNPster weighted mean."""
    stats = summarize_individual_effects(models_df, metric_col)
    if stats is None:
        return ""

    effect_rows = models_df.copy()
    effect_rows["_effect_numeric"] = pd.to_numeric(
        effect_rows[metric_col],
        errors="coerce",
    )
    effect_rows = effect_rows[
        effect_rows["_effect_numeric"].notna()
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    n = stats["n"]
    track_class = " multi-model" if n >= 3 else ""

    max_abs_candidates = [
        abs(float(stats["min"])),
        abs(float(stats["max"])),
        1.0,
    ]
    if not pd.isna(stats["snpster_mean"]):
        max_abs_candidates.append(abs(float(stats["snpster_mean"])))

    axis_limit = max(max_abs_candidates) * 1.15
    axis_low = -axis_limit
    axis_high = axis_limit
    axis_span = axis_high - axis_low

    def pos(x):
        return max(
            0.0,
            min(
                100.0,
                ((float(x) - axis_low) / axis_span) * 100.0,
            ),
        )

    min_pos = pos(stats["min"])
    max_pos = pos(stats["max"])
    q1_pos = pos(stats["q1"])
    q3_pos = pos(stats["q3"])
    median_pos = pos(stats["median"])

    range_color_class = (
        "fill-increased"
        if stats["median"] > 0
        else "fill-lowered"
    )

    range_html = ""
    iqr_html = ""
    point_html = []

    if n >= 2:
        range_left = min(min_pos, max_pos)
        range_width = abs(max_pos - min_pos)
        range_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-distribution-range '
            f'{range_color_class}" '
            f'title="Observed range" '
            f'style="left: {range_left:.2f}%; '
            f'width: {range_width:.2f}%;"></div>'
        )

    if n >= 3:
        iqr_left = min(q1_pos, q3_pos)
        iqr_width = abs(q3_pos - q1_pos)
        iqr_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-distribution-iqr" '
            f'title="Interquartile range" '
            f'style="left: {iqr_left:.2f}%; '
            f'width: {iqr_width:.2f}%;"></div>'
        )

    if n >= 2:
        vertical_offsets = (
            # Keep dense points inside the taller IQR envelope.
            [10, 17, 8, 19, 12, 15, 9, 18]
            if n >= 3
            else [0, 6]
        )

        for i, row in effect_rows.iterrows():
            value = float(row["_effect_numeric"])
            top = vertical_offsets[i % len(vertical_offsets)]
            pgs_id = html.escape(
                str(row.get("pgs_id", "Polygenic score"))
            )
            endpoint = row.get("specific_trait", np.nan)
            endpoint_text = (
                html.escape(str(endpoint))
                if not pd.isna(endpoint) and str(endpoint).strip()
                else "Unspecified outcome"
            )

            study_key, study_label = performance_study_identity(row)
            point_color = study_color(study_key)

            point_html.append(
                f'<span class="effect-distribution-point" '
                f'title="{pgs_id} · {html.escape(study_label)} · '
                f'{endpoint_text}: {html.escape(percent_change_text(value))}" '
                f'style="--study-color: {point_color}; '
                f'left: {pos(value):.2f}%; top: {top}px;"></span>'
            )

    snpster_marker_html = ""
    if n >= 2 and not pd.isna(stats["snpster_mean"]):
        snpster_marker_html = (
            f'<div class="effect-distribution-snpster-mean" '
            f'title="SNPster weighted mean: '
            f'{html.escape(percent_change_text(stats["snpster_mean"]))}" '
            f'style="left: {pos(stats["snpster_mean"]):.2f}%;"></div>'
        )

    median_label = "Estimate" if n == 1 else "Median"



    return f"""
    <div class="effect-distribution"
         aria-label="{html.escape(metric_name)} across ancestry-matched performance estimates">
      <div class="effect-distribution-track{track_class}">
        <div class="effect-distribution-axis"></div>
        {range_html}
        {iqr_html}
        <div class="effect-distribution-zero"
             title="No change (0%)"
             style="left: 50%;"></div>
        {''.join(point_html)}
        <div class="effect-distribution-median"
             title="{median_label}: {html.escape(percent_change_text(stats['median']))}"
             style="left: {median_pos:.2f}%;"></div>
        {snpster_marker_html}
      </div>
      {effect_axis_labels(axis_low, axis_high)}
    </div>
    """



def make_effect_bar_panel(label, models_df, metric_col, raw_col, ratio_label):
    """Render a flat OR/HR-derived risk section directly below the percentile scale."""
    value, caption, stats = effect_summary_display(
        models_df,
        metric_col,
        raw_col,
        ratio_label,
    )

    if stats is None:
        return ""

    visual = make_effect_distribution(models_df, metric_col, label)

    return f"""
    <div class="effect-bar-panel">
      <div class="effect-bar-topline">
        <div class="effect-bar-label">{html.escape(label)}</div>
        <div class="effect-bar-value">{html.escape(value)}</div>
      </div>
      {visual}
      <div class="effect-bar-caption">{html.escape(caption)}</div>
    </div>
    """




data = add_ranking_columns(data)

# Hard report-wide QC filter:
# PGS models with <70% matched variants (or missing variant-match data)
# are removed before family assignment, model agreement, consensus
# calculations, overview figures, card construction, and metadata.
before_variant_filter_rows = len(data)
before_variant_filter_pgs = data["pgs_id"].nunique()

data = data[
    data["variant_match_pct_for_ranking"].ge(MIN_PRIMARY_VARIANT_MATCH_PCT)
].copy()

after_variant_filter_rows = len(data)
after_variant_filter_pgs = data["pgs_id"].nunique()

print(
    f"Dropped {before_variant_filter_pgs - after_variant_filter_pgs} PGS models "
    f"({before_variant_filter_rows - after_variant_filter_rows} rows) with "
    f"<{MIN_PRIMARY_VARIANT_MATCH_PCT:.0f}% matched variants or missing match data."
)

data = assign_report_family_ids(data)
data = data.drop_duplicates()


def split_ontology_values(value):
    """Return unique pipe/comma/semicolon-delimited ontology values."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return []

    raw = str(value).strip()
    if not raw:
        return []

    values = []
    seen = set()

    for token in re.split(r"[|,;]+", raw):
        normalized = token.strip()
        if not normalized:
            continue

        key = normalized.casefold()
        if key in seen:
            continue

        seen.add(key)
        values.append(normalized)

    return values


def canonical_ontology_set(values):
    """Represent ontology identifiers as a deterministic unordered set."""
    if not values:
        return None

    unique = {
        str(value).strip().casefold(): str(value).strip()
        for value in values
        if str(value).strip()
    }

    if not unique:
        return None

    return "|".join(
        sorted(
            unique.values(),
            key=str.casefold,
        )
    )


def core_ontology_ids(value):
    """Select the ontology IDs that define the card's underlying trait.

    MONDO terms are disease/condition anchors. When MONDO is present,
    accompanying EFO, HP, or PATO terms are treated as contextual
    modifiers and do not create a separate card.

    Without MONDO, PATO terms are ignored when another ontology term is
    available because they commonly encode modifiers such as male/female.
    """
    ontology_ids = split_ontology_values(value)

    if not ontology_ids:
        return []

    mondo_ids = [
        ontology_id
        for ontology_id in ontology_ids
        if ontology_id.upper().startswith("MONDO_")
    ]

    if mondo_ids:
        return mondo_ids

    non_pato_ids = [
        ontology_id
        for ontology_id in ontology_ids
        if not ontology_id.upper().startswith("PATO_")
    ]

    if non_pato_ids:
        return non_pato_ids

    # Preserve a PATO-only mapping rather than discarding all metadata.
    return ontology_ids


# Conservative corrections for known metadata variants.
#
# Add entries only when the traits should genuinely be represented in the
# same consumer-facing card. These overrides take precedence over ontology
# IDs because an overly broad or incorrect ontology mapping can otherwise
# bridge unrelated scores transitively.
TRAIT_FAMILY_OVERRIDES = {
    "vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor high bp": "hypertension",
    "essential (primary hypertension) (time-to-event)": "hypertension",
    "essential hypertension": "hypertension",
    "hypertension": "hypertension",

    "heart failure": "heart_failure",
    "congestive heart failure (chf), nos (phecode 428.1)": "heart_failure",
}

TRAIT_FAMILY_DISPLAY_TITLES = {
    "hypertension": "Hypertension",
    "heart_failure": "Heart failure",
}


def normalized_trait_override_key(value):
    """Normalize reported_trait only for lookup in the curated alias map."""
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    normalized = re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip(),
    ).casefold()

    return normalized or None


def curated_trait_family(row):
    """Return a manually curated trait family when one is configured."""
    if row is None:
        return None

    candidates = [
        row.get("reported_trait", np.nan),
        row.get("source_reported_trait", np.nan),
    ]

    for candidate in candidates:
        normalized = normalized_trait_override_key(candidate)
        if not normalized:
            continue

        family = TRAIT_FAMILY_OVERRIDES.get(normalized)
        if family:
            return family

    return None


def curated_trait_family_key(row):
    """Return the authoritative card key for a curated trait family."""
    family = curated_trait_family(row)
    return f"CURATED_FAMILY::{family}" if family else None


def ontology_card_key(row):
    """Return the ontology-aware key for one score, when available."""
    core_ids = core_ontology_ids(
        row.get("efo_id", np.nan)
    )
    ontology_key = canonical_ontology_set(core_ids)

    if ontology_key:
        return f"ONTOLOGY::{ontology_key.casefold()}"

    efo_label_key = canonical_ontology_set(
        split_ontology_values(
            row.get("mapped_trait_efo_label", np.nan)
        )
    )
    if efo_label_key:
        return f"EFO_LABEL::{efo_label_key.casefold()}"

    return None


def exact_reported_trait_key(value):
    """Return a key only for an exact non-empty reported_trait string.

    Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. The remaining text is not
    case-folded or synonym-normalized.
    """
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return None

    trait = str(value).strip()
    if not trait:
        return None

    return f"REPORTED_TRAIT_EXACT::{trait}"


def assign_card_cluster_ids(df):
    """Cluster scores within each report_name section only."""
    if df is None or df.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype="object")

    output = pd.Series(index=df.index, dtype="object")

    for report_name, panel_df in df.groupby(
        "report_name",
        sort=False,
        dropna=False,
    ):
        score_metadata = (
            panel_df[
                [
                    "pgs_id",
                    "efo_id",
                    "mapped_trait_efo_label",
                    "reported_trait",
                ]
            ]
            .drop_duplicates(subset=["pgs_id"], keep="first")
            .copy()
        )

        score_ids = score_metadata["pgs_id"].astype(str).tolist()
        parent = {score_id: score_id for score_id in score_ids}
        rank = {score_id: 0 for score_id in score_ids}

        def find(score_id):
            while parent[score_id] != score_id:
                parent[score_id] = parent[parent[score_id]]
                score_id = parent[score_id]
            return score_id

        def union(left, right):
            left_root = find(left)
            right_root = find(right)

            if left_root == right_root:
                return

            if rank[left_root] < rank[right_root]:
                parent[left_root] = right_root
            elif rank[left_root] > rank[right_root]:
                parent[right_root] = left_root
            else:
                parent[right_root] = left_root
                rank[left_root] += 1

        first_score_for_key = {}

        for _, row in score_metadata.iterrows():
            score_id = str(row["pgs_id"])
            curated_key = curated_trait_family_key(row)

            if curated_key:
                matching_keys = [
                    curated_key,
                    exact_reported_trait_key(
                        row.get("reported_trait", np.nan)
                    ),
                ]
            else:
                matching_keys = [
                    ontology_card_key(row),
                    exact_reported_trait_key(
                        row.get("reported_trait", np.nan)
                    ),
                ]

            for matching_key in matching_keys:
                if not matching_key:
                    continue

                previous_score = first_score_for_key.get(
                    matching_key
                )

                if previous_score is None:
                    first_score_for_key[matching_key] = score_id
                else:
                    union(score_id, previous_score)

        components = {}
        for score_id in score_ids:
            root = find(score_id)
            components.setdefault(root, []).append(score_id)

        panel_text = (
            "Unassigned"
            if report_name is None or pd.isna(report_name)
            else str(report_name).strip()
        )
        panel_slug = re.sub(
            r"[^a-z0-9]+",
            "-",
            panel_text.casefold(),
        ).strip("-") or "section"

        cluster_id_by_score = {}

        for component_scores in components.values():
            sorted_scores = sorted(
                component_scores,
                key=str.casefold,
            )
            cluster_id = (
                f"PANEL::{panel_slug}::CARD::"
                f"{sorted_scores[0].casefold()}"
            )

            for score_id in component_scores:
                cluster_id_by_score[score_id] = cluster_id

        output.loc[panel_df.index] = (
            panel_df["pgs_id"]
            .astype(str)
            .map(cluster_id_by_score)
        )

    return output


def human_card_title(primary, cluster_df):
    """Keep a stable human-readable trait name as the visible card title."""
    curated_families = {
        family
        for family in cluster_df.apply(
            curated_trait_family,
            axis=1,
        )
        if family
    }

    if len(curated_families) == 1:
        family = next(iter(curated_families))
        preferred_title = TRAIT_FAMILY_DISPLAY_TITLES.get(family)
        if preferred_title:
            return preferred_title

    if primary is not None:
        primary_title = primary.get("reported_trait", np.nan)
        if (
            primary_title is not None
            and not pd.isna(primary_title)
            and str(primary_title).strip()
        ):
            return str(primary_title).strip()

    candidates = (
        cluster_df["reported_trait"]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )
    candidates = candidates[candidates.ne("")]

    if not candidates.empty:
        # Prefer the most frequent label. Resolve ties by shortest label,
        # then alphabetically for deterministic output.
        counts = candidates.value_counts()
        highest_count = counts.max()
        tied = counts[counts.eq(highest_count)].index.tolist()
        return sorted(
            tied,
            key=lambda value: (
                len(value),
                value.casefold(),
            ),
        )[0]

    mapped_labels = (
        cluster_df["mapped_trait_efo_label"]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )
    mapped_labels = mapped_labels[mapped_labels.ne("")]

    if not mapped_labels.empty:
        return mapped_labels.iloc[0]

    return "Polygenic trait"


data["card_cluster_id"] = assign_card_cluster_ids(
    data
)

# One display card per connected trait group.
#
# Scores are joined when either their ontology-aware core key matches or
# their trimmed reported_trait strings are exactly identical. These links
# are transitive.
#
# Ontology examples:
#   MONDO_0005291|PATO_0000383 -> MONDO_0005291
#   MONDO_0005291|PATO_0000384 -> MONDO_0005291
#   EFO_0007659|MONDO_0004975 -> MONDO_0004975
#
# The card title remains a human-readable reported_trait from the selected
# primary PGS rather than exposing an ontology identifier to the reader.
#
# Two data levels are deliberately kept separate:
#
#   PGS level
#   ---------
#   One row per retained PGS. Percentile, z-score, variant match, model
#   agreement, family weighting, and the primary-model role are calculated here.
#   Validation discrimination is the mean across that PGS's ancestry-matched
#   PPM discrimination values.
#
#   PPM level
#   ---------
#   Every ancestry-matched PPM is retained. If a PPM reports an OR or HR, that
#   PPM contributes its own point to the corresponding effect plot. This means
#   stratified outcomes from pgs_performance remain visible rather than being
#   discarded during a one-row-per-PGS collapse.
card_records = []

for (
    report_name,
    cluster_id,
), cluster_df in data.groupby(
    ["report_name", "card_cluster_id"],
    sort=True,
    dropna=False,
):
    trait_ppms = cluster_df.copy()

    trait_models = summarize_rows_per_pgs(trait_ppms)
    trait_models = sort_for_primary_model(trait_models)

    primary = best_primary_model_row(
        trait_models,
        require_primary_eligible=True,
    )

    if primary is None:
        continue

    card_title = human_card_title(
        primary,
        trait_ppms,
    )

    retained_pgs_ids = trait_models["pgs_id"].astype(str).tolist()

    odds_ppms = valid_metric_ppms(
        trait_ppms,
        "individual_odds_ratio",
        retained_pgs_ids,
    )

    hazard_ppms = valid_metric_ppms(
        trait_ppms,
        "individual_hazard_ratio",
        retained_pgs_ids,
    )

    retained_ppms = trait_ppms[
        trait_ppms["pgs_id"].astype(str).isin(retained_pgs_ids)
        & trait_ppms["primary_model_eligible"].fillna(False)
    ].copy()

    cluster_families = {
        family
        for family in trait_ppms.apply(
            curated_trait_family,
            axis=1,
        )
        if family
    }
    curated_family = (
        next(iter(cluster_families))
        if len(cluster_families) == 1
        else None
    )

    card_records.append({
        "report_name": (
            "Other Health Conditions"
            if report_name is None or pd.isna(report_name)
            else str(report_name).strip()
        ),
        "card_cluster_id": cluster_id,
        "curated_trait_family": curated_family,
        "core_ontology_id": canonical_ontology_set(
            core_ontology_ids(
                primary.get("efo_id", np.nan)
            )
        ),
        "efo_id": primary.get("efo_id", np.nan),
        "mapped_trait_efo_label": primary.get(
            "mapped_trait_efo_label",
            np.nan,
        ),
        "reported_trait": card_title,
        "primary": primary,
        "odds_models": odds_ppms,
        "hazard_models": hazard_ppms,
        "all_models": trait_models,
        "all_ppms": retained_ppms,
    })

cards_df = pd.DataFrame([
```

```{python}
def overview_classify_agreement_spread(spread_width):
    """Self-contained agreement classifier for the overview block."""
    spread_width = float(spread_width)

    if spread_width < 5:
        return "Very high"
    if spread_width < 10:
        return "High"
    if spread_width < 20:
        return "Moderate"
    if spread_width <= 25:
        return "Low"
    return "Very low"


def overview_record_context(record):
    """Classify one trait for report ordering before later helpers are defined."""
    primary = record["primary"]
    all_models = record["all_models"]
    all_ppms = record["all_ppms"]

    values = pd.to_numeric(
        all_models["percentile_norm2"],
        errors="coerce",
    ).dropna()

    n_models = int(len(all_models))
    is_single = n_models <= 1

    display_percentile = display_percentile_for_column(
        primary,
        all_models,
        "percentile_norm2",
    )

    if len(values) <= 1:
        agreement_status = "Not assessable"
    else:
        spread = (
            float(values.quantile(0.75) - values.quantile(0.25))
            if len(values) > 4
            else float(values.max() - values.min())
        )
        agreement_status = overview_classify_agreement_spread(spread)

    moderate_or_better = agreement_status in {
        "Very high",
        "High",
        "Moderate",
    }

    if is_single:
        section = "single"
    elif moderate_or_better:
        section = "multi_supported"
    else:
        section = "low_agreement"

    return {
        "display_percentile": display_percentile,
        "agreement_status": agreement_status,
        "section": section,
    }

single_records = [

ANCESTRY_COMPONENTS = [
    ("eur", "EUR", "European", "#9FC4E7"),
    ("eas", "EAS", "East Asian", "#F3C6A8"),
    ("sas", "SAS", "South Asian", "#E9B7CF"),

]


def make_ancestry_profile(row, primary_code):
    """Render the user's ancestry fractions as a radial sunburst-style chart."""
    if row is None:
        return ""

    components = []

    for column, code, label, color in ANCESTRY_COMPONENTS:
        value = pd.to_numeric(
            pd.Series([row.get(column, np.nan)]),
            errors="coerce",
        ).iloc[0]

        if pd.isna(value) or float(value) <= 0:
            continue

        components.append({
            "column": column,
            "code": code,
            "label": label,
            "color": color,
            "fraction": float(value),
        })

    if not components:
        return ""

    total = sum(item["fraction"] for item in components)
    if total <= 0:
        return ""

    # Normalize the geometry to a complete circle while displaying the original
    # database fractions in the legend.
    current_degrees = 0.0
    gradient_parts = []

    for item in components:
        visual_share = item["fraction"] / total
        start = current_degrees
        end = current_degrees + visual_share * 360.0
        gradient_parts.append(
            f"{item['color']} {start:.3f}deg {end:.3f}deg"
        )
        current_degrees = end

    gradient = "conic-gradient(" + ", ".join(gradient_parts) + ")"

    sorted_components = sorted(
        components,
        key=lambda item: (-item["fraction"], item["label"]),
    )

    legend_items = []
    for item in sorted_components:
        legend_items.append(
            f"""
            <div class="ancestry-profile-legend-item">
              <span
                class="ancestry-profile-swatch"
                style="--ancestry-color: {item['color']};"
                aria-hidden="true"
              ></span>
              <span class="ancestry-profile-name">
                {html.escape(item['label'])}
              </span>
              <span class="ancestry-profile-percent">
                {item['fraction'] * 100:.1f}%
              </span>
            </div>
            """
        )

    primary_component = next(
        (
            item
            for item in components
            if item["code"] == primary_code
        ),
        max(components, key=lambda item: item["fraction"]),
    )

    primary_fraction = row.get(
        "primary_ancestry_percentage",
        np.nan,
    )
    primary_fraction = pd.to_numeric(
        pd.Series([primary_fraction]),
        errors="coerce",
    ).iloc[0]

    if pd.isna(primary_fraction):
        primary_fraction = primary_component["fraction"]

    ancestry_method = first_nonempty_value(
        row,
        ["ancestry_method"],
    )
    reference_panel = first_nonempty_value(
        row,
        ["reference_panel"],
    )

    metadata_bits = [
        value
        for value in [
            ancestry_method,
            reference_panel,
        ]
        if value
    ]
    metadata_text = " · ".join(metadata_bits)

    return f"""
    <div class="ancestry-profile-card">
      <div class="ancestry-profile-visual">
        <div class="ancestry-sunburst-wrap">
          <div
            class="ancestry-sunburst"
            style="--ancestry-gradient: {gradient};"
            role="img"
            aria-label="Genetic ancestry composition"
          >
            <div class="ancestry-sunburst-core">
              <div class="ancestry-sunburst-primary-value">
                {float(primary_fraction) * 100:.1f}%
              </div>
              <div class="ancestry-sunburst-primary-label">
                {html.escape(primary_component['label'])}<br>
                primary ancestry
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="ancestry-profile-copy">
        <div class="ancestry-profile-kicker">Genetic ancestry</div>
        <div class="ancestry-profile-title">Ancestry composition</div>
        <div class="ancestry-profile-subtitle">
          Estimated ancestry fractions used for population context. Validation
          evidence is retained for every ancestry component above 20%.
        </div>

        <div class="ancestry-profile-legend">
          {''.join(legend_items)}
        </div>

        <div class="ancestry-profile-note">
          <strong>Small ancestry components:</strong>
          values around 5% or less are often low-confidence and may reflect
          reference/model noise. Treat them as trace signals unless supported
          by other ancestry evidence.
        </div>

        {
            f'<div class="ancestry-profile-meta">{html.escape(metadata_text)}</div>'
            if metadata_text
            else ''
        }
      </div>
    </div>
    """


ancestry_profile_html = make_ancestry_profile(

def report_anchor_slug(value):
    text_value = str(value).strip().casefold()
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text_value).strip("-")
    return f"health-section-{slug or 'other'}"


PANEL_STYLE_HUES = [
    214, 278, 154, 34, 188, 326,
    92, 258, 16, 174, 48, 204,
    122, 296, 66, 238, 346,
]


def panel_style(panel_index):
    hue = PANEL_STYLE_HUES[
        panel_index % len(PANEL_STYLE_HUES)
    ]
    return {
        "accent": f"hsl({hue}, 38%, 46%)",
        "soft": f"hsla({hue}, 58%, 95%, .93)",
        "border": f"hsla({hue}, 40%, 60%, .25)",
        "divider": f"hsla({hue}, 40%, 48%, .30)",
    }


def panel_risk_counts(records):
    """Count high/low results for the introduction navigation.

    This function runs before the detailed card-rendering helpers are defined,
    so it deliberately uses overview_record_context(), which is already
    available in the introduction chunk and uses the same ancestry-standardized
    display-percentile logic.
    """
    high = 0
    low = 0

    for record in records:
        percentile = overview_record_context(
            record
        )["display_percentile"]

        if percentile is None or pd.isna(percentile):
            continue

        percentile = float(percentile)

        if percentile >= 80:
            high += 1
        elif percentile < 20:
            low += 1

    return high, low

  <div class="panel-index-copy">

    <div class="panel-index-description">
      Equal-trait mean of the displayed percentiles. This is a descriptive
      profile index, not a combined clinical-risk or disease-burden score.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
"""


# Build a compact percentile spectrum across all displayed traits.
spectrum_points = []

for record, context in story_contexts:
    percentile = max(
        0.0,
        min(100.0, float(context["display_percentile"])),
    )
    trait = str(record["reported_trait"])
    risk_label, risk_class, _ = risk_level(percentile)

    if context["section"] == "multi_supported":
        evidence_class = "supported"
        evidence_label = "Multi-PGS · Moderate-or-better agreement"
    elif context["section"] == "single":
        evidence_class = "single"
        evidence_label = "Single PGS"
    else:
        evidence_class = "low-agreement"
        evidence_label = "Multi-PGS · Low or Very low agreement"

    spectrum_points.append({
        "trait": trait,
        "percentile": percentile,
        "risk_label": risk_label,
        "risk_class": risk_class,
        "agreement_status": context["agreement_status"],
        "evidence_class": evidence_class,
        "evidence_label": evidence_label,
    })


# Deterministically assign nearby points to separate vertical lanes.
# This keeps the spectrum compact while reducing marker overlap.
n_lanes = 7
min_horizontal_gap = 3.0
lane_last_percentile = [-999.0] * n_lanes

for point in sorted(
    spectrum_points,
    key=lambda item: (
        item["percentile"],
        item["trait"].lower(),
    ),
):
    available_lanes = [
        lane
        for lane in range(n_lanes)
        if point["percentile"] - lane_last_percentile[lane] >= min_horizontal_gap
    ]

    if available_lanes:
        lane = available_lanes[0]
    else:
        lane = min(
            range(n_lanes),
            key=lambda idx: lane_last_percentile[idx],
        )

    point["lane"] = lane
    lane_last_percentile[lane] = point["percentile"]


point_html = []

for point in spectrum_points:
    display_left = max(
        0.8,
        min(99.2, point["percentile"]),
    )
    top = 8 + point["lane"] * 12

    tooltip = (
        f"{point['trait']} · {fmt_percentile(point['percentile'])} percentile · "
        f"{point['risk_label']} · {point['evidence_label']} · "
        f"Model agreement: {point['agreement_status']}"
    )

    point_html.append(
        f'<span class="profile-spectrum-point '
        f'profile-spectrum-point-{html.escape(point["evidence_class"])} '
        f'profile-spectrum-risk-{html.escape(point["risk_class"])}" '
        f'title="{html.escape(tooltip)}" '
        f'style="left: {display_left:.2f}%; top: {top}px;"></span>'
    )


n_lower_percentile = sum(
    point["percentile"] < 20
    for point in spectrum_points
)
n_typical_percentile = sum(
    20 <= point["percentile"] < 80
    for point in spectrum_points
)
n_higher_percentile = sum(
    point["percentile"] >= 80
    for point in spectrum_points
)

spectrum_html = f"""
<div class="profile-spectrum">
  <div class="profile-spectrum-header">
    <div>
      <div class="profile-spectrum-title">Your percentile profile across evaluated traits</div>
      <div class="profile-spectrum-subtitle">
        Each marker represents one trait positioned by its ancestry-standardized genetic percentile.
        Hover over a marker to see the trait, percentile, risk category, and model agreement.
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="profile-spectrum-counts">
      <span class="profile-spectrum-count"><strong>{n_lower_percentile}</strong> lower</span>
      <span class="profile-spectrum-count"><strong>{n_typical_percentile}</strong> typical</span>
      <span class="profile-spectrum-count"><strong>{n_higher_percentile}</strong> higher</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="profile-spectrum-plot" aria-label="Overview of trait percentiles from 0 to 100">
    <div class="profile-spectrum-baseline"></div>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-boundary" style="left: 5%;"></span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-boundary" style="left: 20%;"></span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-boundary" style="left: 80%;"></span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-boundary" style="left: 95%;"></span>
    {''.join(point_html)}
  </div>

  <div class="profile-spectrum-axis">
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label edge-left" style="left: 0%;">0</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label" style="left: 5%;">5</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label" style="left: 20%;">20</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label" style="left: 50%;">50</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label" style="left: 80%;">80</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label" style="left: 95%;">95</span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-axis-label edge-right" style="left: 100%;">100</span>
  </div>

  <div class="profile-spectrum-bands">
    <div class="profile-spectrum-band">Very low</div>
    <div class="profile-spectrum-band">Lowered</div>
    <div class="profile-spectrum-band">Typical</div>
    <div class="profile-spectrum-band">Increased</div>
    <div class="profile-spectrum-band">Highly increased</div>
  </div>

  <div class="profile-spectrum-legend">
    <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-item">
      <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-dot"></span>
      Multi-PGS · Moderate-or-better agreement
    </span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-item">
      <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-ring"></span>
      Single PGS
    </span>
    <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-item">
      <span class="profile-spectrum-legend-diamond"></span>
      Below-Moderate model agreement
    </span>
  </div>
</div>
"""

results_summary_html = f"""
<section
  class="results-summary-shell report-tab-panel"
  data-report-tab="intro"
  id="results-summary"
>
  <div class="results-summary-heading">
    <div>
      <div class="results-summary-kicker">Results Summary</div>
      <div class="results-summary-title">Your profile at a glance</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  {panel_index_orb_html}

  {spectrum_html}

  {summary_html}
</section>
"""

display(HTML(
    report_tabs_html
    + report_header_html
    + report_navigation_html
    + panel_navigation_html
))
```

```{=html}
  <div class="reader-guide-content">
    <div class="reader-guide-intro">
      The main percentile is ancestry-standardized continuously rather than
      forcing you into one population label. This is especially useful for
      mixed or underrepresented ancestry, although reference-panel limitations
      still remain. The report describes inherited predisposition only and is
      not a diagnosis.
    </div>

    <div class="reader-guide-principles">
      <div class="reader-guide-principle">
        <strong>A percentile is a ranking</strong>
        <span>
          It shows where your genetic score sits relative to other people.
          It is not your percentage chance of developing a condition.
        </span>
      </div>
      <div class="reader-guide-principle">
```
